video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about lengths of time, clocks and measuring how long async work takes: Duration, Clock & ContinuousClock, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Duration - A length of time, such as seconds or milliseconds, stored as a precise value.
Clock - A protocol for something that tells the time and can wait until a given moment.
ContinuousClock - A clock that keeps counting even while the device sleeps, handy for measuring elapsed time.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Duration, Clock & ContinuousClock in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Duration, Clock, ContinuousClock 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Duration - A length of time, such as seconds or milliseconds, stored as a precise value.
한국어: Duration: 초나 밀리초 같은 시간의 길이를 정확한 값으로 담는 타입

Clock - A protocol for something that tells the time and can wait until a given moment.
한국어: Clock: 시간을 알려 주고 정해진 시점까지 기다릴 수 있는 것을 나타내는 프로토콜

ContinuousClock - A clock that keeps counting even while the device sleeps, handy for measuring elapsed time.
한국어: ContinuousClock: 기기가 잠자는 동안에도 계속 흐르는 시계로, 경과 시간을 재는 데 편리함

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about measuring and waiting with time values instead of plain numbers, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Duration, Clock and ContinuousClock in English?

dialogue.title: No more magic numbers for time
dialogue.setting: Replacing nanosecond numbers in a retry helper

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my retry helper waits for `1_000_000_000`. Nobody knows what that means.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is nanoseconds. Use a Duration instead. Write `.seconds(1)`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So a Duration is a length of time with a unit?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and it prints nicely, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I also want to test the helper without waiting one real second.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then take a Clock as a parameter. In the app you pass the real one, and in tests a fake one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And which real clock do I use to measure the request time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A ContinuousClock. Call `measure` and it returns a Duration.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does it stop when the phone sleeps?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. A ContinuousClock keeps counting, so it shows real elapsed time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. Duration for the delay, Clock for tests, ContinuousClock for timing.
Use a Duration instead of a plain number.
